method.label: Count lengths on both sides of the altitude

annotationRationale: The perpendicular gives the minimum distance, and the Pythagorean theorem controls how distances increase on each side of its foot. The triangle area formula supplies the altitude's length.
sourceMethod: Follows the official altitude-and-area solution, adding a Pythagorean explanation of why each eligible length occurs exactly once on each applicable side.

review.mathCheck: AC=29 and BD=420/29 lies between 14 and 15. On DA, distances increase to 20; on DC, they increase to 21. Lengths 15–20 each occur twice and 21 once, totaling 13, choice D, including both legs.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded adaptation of MAA Q16, page 7, consistent with its figure. It preserves the altitude-and-area method and explains the two occurrences of each eligible length.
review.annotationCheck: The Pythagorean distance formula justifies monotonicity and exhaustive counting. The interior minimum and both endpoints are handled.
